facts.fact: Mozambique is the only country in the world whose name contains all five vowels exactly once.
facts.flagElement: five small circles arranged in a pentagon pattern in the upper left, each a different color representing the vowels

facts.fact: The country is home to the extraordinary coconut crab, the world's largest land-living arthropod that can crack coconuts with its massive claws.
facts.flagElement: a bold white crab silhouette in the center of the flag

facts.fact: Mozambique's coast is famous for the ancient dhow sailing vessels that have connected East Africa to Arabia and India for over a thousand years.
facts.flagElement: a triangular sail shape on the right side, representing a traditional dhow

decoys.overlap: Good thinking — Oman has an ancient dhow sailing tradition connecting the Arabian Peninsula to East Africa. But Oman's coast isn't known for giant coconut crabs, and its name doesn't have that special vowel pattern.

You're on to something — the Seychelles islands are indeed famous for coconut crabs living on their shores. However, this island nation doesn't have the dhow maritime heritage or the unique vowel pattern in its name.
Smart guess — Tanzania's coast does have historical dhow sailing culture along the Indian Ocean. But it doesn't have the distinctive vowel arrangement in its name, and isn't known for coconut crabs.
